title: Allow toggling camera access through camera indicator
line: The camera indicator now has an "Allow camera access" switch that makes the system refuse the camera to apps that ask for it.
explanation: Plasma had no place to switch the camera off: the camera indicator only listed PipeWire cameras. The desktop portal already refuses camera requests when its Lockdown backend sets disable-camera (that is what GNOME's camera privacy switch uses), but xdg-desktop-portal-kde never implemented Lockdown, and Qt D-Bus can't export its dash-named properties through a normal adaptor. xdg-desktop-portal-kde now serves the Lockdown interface on a second connection (name org.freedesktop.impl.portal.desktop.kde.lockdown, new kde-lockdown.portal, D-Bus activatable) and stores the values in xdg-desktop-portal-kderc; kde-portals.conf points Lockdown at it. The camera indicator gets an "Allow camera access" switch in its header (also in its right-click menu) that sets disable-camera, shows "Camera access is blocked" and stays in the tray while blocked so it can be turned back on.

commits.message:
lockdown: implement the Lockdown portal backend

The portal frontend refuses camera, microphone and other requests when
the Lockdown backend says so, but we had none. Serve its dash-named
properties from a connection of our own and keep them in our config.

BUG: 447034

applets/cameraindicator: add a switch to allow or block camera access

The camera indicator had no way to refuse the camera to apps. Its new
switch sets the portal's disable-camera lockdown, and the indicator
stays visible while access is blocked so that it can be turned back on.

BUG: 447034

media.caption: Before: the camera indicator only lists cameras, with no way to block them
After: an "Allow camera access" switch in the indicator's header
Switched off: the portal now refuses camera requests ("Camera access disabled")
While blocked the indicator stays in the tray with a crossed-out camera and says so
The same toggle in the indicator's right-click menu
